facts.statement: If the payload ran in your repository, assume every secret and cloud role available to its workflows is compromised.

editorial.title: wfx-loot turns stolen GitHub access into CI credential theft
editorial.summary: Aikido reports stolen GitHub credentials were used to inject secret-stealing workflows and install hooks into repositories from November 10. Probe pull requests do not prove every repository executed the payload; deleted run logs can hide execution.
editorial.why_it_matters: A CI compromise can expose workflow secrets, cloud identities and publishing access. A clean current branch does not establish that earlier runs were clean.
editorial.action: Audit suspicious branches, workflow history and OIDC changes. If the payload ran, treat workflow-accessible credentials as exposed and investigate persistence before restoring trust.
